segments.text: Hi there. Today we are going to see machine  learning CPU versus GPU. And in this video
I'll show you what is the difference in terms of  architecture, in terms of algorithm as well as
in terms of performance. So the business case  which I have for you today is we have a bank
uh which would like to use uh machine learning to  train a model which can predict a loan payback and
the data which is being used is something like  this. So you have uh all the data for the past
loan applications and this data has got the annual  income. It has got the depth to income ratio,
the credit score, loan amount, interest rate uh  as well as it has got information regarding the
loan applicant. In addition, it also has got  this column loan paid back which is one and
zero. One means  the loan was paid back in  the past and zero means it was not paid back.
So you can use this data to train a machine  learning model. Let us first see on how you
can do that on a CPU. So first of all you need  to identify what are the X and Y variable. So
Y variable here is the target variable. It means  the variable which we want to predict which is the
loan paid back and all other columns which you saw  in the previous  table are the X. Then you need
to identify what are the numerical columns  and what are the categorical columns and then
you have to apply some  transformations. So for  all the numerical columns you have to scale them.
It means you have to convert them into values  between 0 and one. And for all the non-numerical
columns or also called as the categorical columns,  you have to transform them using one hot encoding.
And I'll explain you later on what is this one  hot encoding. And then you can use various machine
learning models and one of the very famous  machine learning models which you can use on a
CPU is a random forest classifier. So you can  train the model. It would look something like
this. You apply uh the standard scaler as well  as one hot encoder and then you apply your model.
Now once you do that you'll get an model accuracy  of  90%. As well as the model training time is
uh quite high. It is almost about 681 seconds  which is roughly 10 minutes which is quite high.
Now let us see on how you can do the same task but  this time using a GPU. So here the GPU which I'm
using is the Apple GPU also called as metal.  So the initial steps are similar. You have to
identify the X and Y and apply this pre-processing  but the difference is in the model training.
So here I'm using a model training library which  is called as pytorch and this is based on a deep
learning architecture and the reason why I'm using  this is because you can train a machine learning
model on a GPU using a deep learning architecture.  So here deep learning architecture you have to
create various layers and it's for this reason  this is called as deep learning and you'll see
a model something like this. You'll have these  different layers of the neural network which
is shown over here and you'll get a model accuracy  of 90% but this time the processing is quite fast.
The complete training gets completed in just 32  seconds which is 200 times faster than the CPU.
So why is there a big difference between the  CPU and GPU? And one of the main reasons is
the volume of data. So the data what we are using  for the loan applications has almost about 500,000
rows which is like half a million rows and also  the logic of one hot encoding increases the
number of column. So for example let's say you  have a column  called as education level and
which has got these three values and when you  apply this one hot encoding it gets converted
into multiple columns all with one or zero. So  in total we have 16 columns and when you apply
this one encoding the training data consist  of 70 columns. So you have a data set which
has got a half a million of lines as well as  70 columns which is quite huge and a GPU would
always excel compared to a CPU when it the data  is very very high. The other factor is that the
deep learning algorithm can also be effectively  parallelized on a GPU which is not possible using
the random forest classifier. So it's for these  two reasons the parallelization of algorithm as
well as the volume of data gives the GPU an edge  over the CPU. Now let us do a quick knowledge
check to see if you understood this concept. So  first of all, what is the common algorithm to
train a machine learning model on a CPU? And  I'll give you one second to think about it.
All right, so answer is random  forest. Second question,
what is an common algorithm to train a machine  learning model but on a GPU? And once again,
I'm going to give you one  second to think about it.
All right. So the answer is deep learning.  Third question, why is a GPU faster than a CPU?
All right, because you can parallelize the  algorithm using a GPU. Thank you for watching.
